  "candidates": [
    {
      "startEvent": 228,
      "endEvent": 234,
      "contextStartEvent": 197,
      "contextEndEvent": 234,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "But if you want to make good people do wicked things, you'll need religion.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["shame"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Hitchens approvingly quotes a general necessity claim. His preceding examples explain how religious prescriptions can motivate harmful acts, but do not establish that religion is required for good people to do harm. The quotation could be rhetorical emphasis on that narrower mechanism; no objection-neutralizing device appears here."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 451,
      "endEvent": 464,
      "contextStartEvent": 307,
      "contextEndEvent": 490,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "it is based essentially on a perversion of faith.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Blair classifies religious evil as perversion and religious good as authentic, insulating his proposed essence from adverse instances. E348–370 supply teachings supporting compassion, but no clear criterion establishes their exclusive authority. His explicit acknowledgment of religious harm means this protects the essence claim, not every claim about religion's effects."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 713,
      "endEvent": 719,
      "contextStartEvent": 658,
      "contextEndEvent": 760,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "That's not a very productive way of of of arguing this.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Rejecting comparison of hospices with a suicide bomber could exclude evidence relevant to religion's overall effects. However, E713–719 may reject only crude arithmetic, while E687–711 carefully limit the motivational claim. This is an uncertain restriction on criticism, not a compact affirmation substituting for an argument."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1003,
      "endEvent": 1008,
      "contextStartEvent": 892,
      "contextEndEvent": 1008,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "And that is genuinely the proper face of faith.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The renewed authenticity formula privileges benevolent motivation after objections about charity. E919–936 and E970–996 provide concrete supporting examples, earning the narrower claim that faith can motivate good. Whether 'proper face' additionally dismisses contrary religious practices by definition is uncertain here; Blair expressly acknowledges negative historical roles."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1093,
      "endEvent": 1099,
      "contextStartEvent": 1048,
      "contextEndEvent": 1122,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "it's a surrender of reason in favor of faith",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["shame"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The formulation supplies a general psychological mechanism for why any faith intensifies division. E1060–1093 offer reasons concerning particular exclusive institutions and identities, but do not establish that every faith entails surrendering reason. Earlier evidence objections support criticism of supernatural claims without earning this unrestricted characterization."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1164,
      "endEvent": 1169,
      "contextStartEvent": 1141,
      "contextEndEvent": 1213,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "True religion is actually about embracing someone who is different.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "In response to divisiveness, Blair explicitly excludes exclusionary conduct from true religion. Neighbor-love teachings at E1170–1186 support an inclusive interpretation, but do not establish why contrary teachings cannot count as authentic. His acknowledgments at E1141–1143 and E1205–1208 preserve criticism of actual religion while protecting the defined essence."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2576,
      "endEvent": 2582,
      "contextStartEvent": 2492,
      "contextEndEvent": 2616,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "you're not really religious if you don't believe that there is a divine supervision involved.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The definition excludes religion without divine supervision from the category being criticized, protecting the universal supervision claim against such counterexamples. Blair's own higher-power belief makes this relevant to their exchange, and E2534–2563 explain the freedom objection. What remains unsupported is extending that definition to religion generally."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2727,
      "endEvent": 2734,
      "contextStartEvent": 2647,
      "contextEndEvent": 2751,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "totally contrary to the true meaning of faith.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Blair renews the distinction that places religious evil outside faith's true meaning. This protects the normative essence from contrary conduct, without supplying a decisive interpretive criterion. However, E2730 explicitly accepts harm as a consequence of religion, and E2714–2717 invite debate; his defense does not make actual religion immune to criticism."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 687,
      "endEvent": 711,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "Of course, it's possible for them to have done it, but the fact is that's what motivated them.",
      "explanation": "Blair distinguishes religious motivation from religion being necessary for good conduct. He supplies the example of nuns caring for children with HIV AIDS and explicitly acknowledges secular goodness, giving his limited conclusion supporting reasons."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2492,
      "endEvent": 2563,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "it wasn't worth it at the sacrifice of mental and intellectual and moral freedom.",
      "explanation": "Hitchens acknowledges communist heroism and achievements before explaining his objection to infallible leadership. The compact conclusion summarizes an explicit tradeoff argument and preserves favorable evidence about the movement he criticizes."
